([[Austroasiatic languages|Austroasiatic]]?) | iso3 = xbn | linglist = xbn.html | glotto = kena1236 | glottorefname = Kenaboi | dia1 = dialect 1 | dia2 = dialect 2 | era = attested c. 1880 | lingua = 31-MFF-af }} '''Kĕnaboi''' is an [[Extinct language|extinct]] unclassified language of [[Negeri Sembilan]], [[Malay Peninsula|Malaysia]] that may be a [[language isolate]] or an [[Austroasiatic languages|Austroasiatic]] language belonging to the [[Aslian languages|Aslian]] branch. It is attested in what appears to be two dialects,[https://web.archive.org/web/20120615142105/http://multitree.linguistlist.org/codes/0m1-kdo 0m1-kdo] in [[MultiTree]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20120615142122/http://multitree.linguistlist.org/codes/0m1-kdt 0m1-kdt] in MultiTree. based on word lists of about 250 lexical items, presumably collected around 1870–90. ==Background== In [[Walter William Skeat (anthropologist)|Walter William Skeat]] and [[Charles Otto Blagden]]'s 1906 work "Pagan Races of the Malay Peninsula",{{harvnb|Skeat|Blagden|1906}} the contents of three previously unpublished wordlists appear, two of which were collected by D.F.A. Hervey, a former government official in Malacca. There is no indication as to when these word lists were collected; however, there is a possibility that these wordlists were collected around the 1870s to 1890s. Hervey collected his Kenaboi lexicon in [[Alor Gajah]], [[Malacca]] from speakers living in [[Mount Datuk|Gunung Dato']],{{harvnb|Skeat|Blagden|1906|pp=497–498}} which is a mountain situated in [[Rembau District]], southern [[Negeri Sembilan]]. Based on the ethnonym, the Kenaboi may have originated from the Kenaboi River valley of [[Jelebu District]], northern Negeri Sembilan (Hajek 1998). Today, the [[Orang Asli]] of Negeri Sembilan are primarily [[Temuan language|Temuan]] speakers. ==Classification== [[John Hajek]] (1998){{harvnb|Hajek|1998}} proposes that Kenaboi is a mixed language of both [[Aslian languages|Aslian]] and [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian]] origins, with Kenaboi (dialect 1) having a higher proportion of Austroasiatic words than Kenaboi (dialect 2). Kenaboi (dialect 1) also has many words of unknown origin, such as {{lang|xbn|mambu}} 'white' and {{lang|xbn|par}} 'water'. Hajek (1998) speculates that the lexical aberrancy of Kenaboi 1 may be due to the fact that Kenaboi 1 was a special [[argot|taboo language]], while Kenaboi 2 was the regular non-taboo language. The lexicon of Kenaboi 1 is 47% Austroasiatic, 27% Austronesian, and 26% unclassified out of a total of 216 words. Hammarström, et al.{{Glottolog|kena1236}} note in [[Glottolog]] that Kenaboi is best considered to be a [[language isolate]], and do not consider arguments of Kenaboi as a taboo-jargon ([[argot]]) to be convincing. Skeat and Blagden (1906) considers Kenaboi as an isolate unrelated to Austroasiatic and Austronesian. [[Rasa language|Rasa]], another extinct language documented in Skeat & Blagden (1906) near [[Rasa, Malaysia|Rasa]] in [[Ulu Selangor]], also has many words of uncertain origin (Phillips 2012: 257-258).{{harvnb|Phillips|2012}} ==See also== *[[Wiktionary:Appendix:Kenaboi word list|Kenaboi word list]] (Wiktionary) *[[Andamanese languages]] *[[Philippine Negrito languages]] *[[Proto-Aslian language]] *[[Kusunda language]] Other Southeast Asian languages with high proportions of unique vocabulary of possible [[language isolate|isolate]] origin: *[[Enggano language]] (Indonesia) *[[Manide language]] (Philippines) *[[Umiray Dumaget language]] (Philippines) ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==References== {{refbegin}} * {{Cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/paganracesofmala02skea_1 |title=Pagan Races of the Malay Peninsula |last1=Skeat |first1=W.
